name: Toledo
takeaway: Toledo is on NOAC at 9.75¢ — repriced from a lower baseline. City is the anchor of a 13-community coalition with a captive rate. Competitive supply can improve on this.
hook: Toledo is locked into the NOAC program at 9.75¢ — have you compared that against what's available in the open market right now?
notes: NOAC (Northwest Ohio Aggregation Coalition) serves 13 communities via Toledo Edison/FirstEnergy. Current supplier: Dynegy at 9.75¢/kWh. Gas: variable NYMEX+$0.2092/Ccf through Apr 2028. NOAC switched from Energy Harbor to Dynegy June 2025. Dynegy contract (8.63¢→9.75¢) ended May 2026. New NOAC contract terms being finalized.

name: Perrysburg
takeaway: Perrysburg is a fast-growing Wood County suburb on NOAC at 9.75¢. Commercial activity along I-75 corridor makes this high-value prospecting territory.
hook: Perrysburg is part of the NOAC coalition — 9.75¢ right now. Worth seeing if we can do better for your commercial accounts.
notes: NOAC member community. Strong commercial growth along US-20 and I-75. Toledo Edison service area. NOAC switched from Energy Harbor to Dynegy June 2025. Dynegy contract (8.63¢→9.75¢) ended May 2026. New NOAC contract terms being finalized.

name: Maumee
takeaway: Maumee is a dense commercial NOAC market at 9.75¢. Arrowhead Road and nearby retail/industrial accounts are active targets.
hook: Maumee is on the NOAC program — 9.75¢. Some of those accounts along Arrowhead haven't looked at alternatives in a while.
notes: NOAC member, Toledo Edison. Strong commercial/industrial base near Arrowhead Road corridor. NOAC switched from Energy Harbor to Dynegy June 2025. Dynegy contract (8.63¢→9.75¢) ended May 2026. New NOAC contract terms being finalized.

name: Sylvania
takeaway: Sylvania is an affluent northwest Toledo suburb in the NOAC program at 9.75¢. Good mix of medical, professional, and retail accounts.
hook: Sylvania is on NOAC — 9.75¢. Are your clients there still on the aggregation program or have they opted out?
notes: NOAC member community, Toledo Edison. Affluent suburb with medical and professional office presence. NOAC switched from Energy Harbor to Dynegy June 2025. Dynegy contract (8.63¢→9.75¢) ended May 2026. New NOAC contract terms being finalized.

name: Oregon
takeaway: Oregon (Lucas County) is a NOAC member at 9.75¢ with significant industrial and refinery-adjacent commercial presence near the Maumee River.
hook: Oregon is on the NOAC coalition at 9.75¢ — do any of your industrial accounts in that area have supply expiring?
notes: NOAC member, Toledo Edison/FirstEnergy. Industrial character — refinery, port, and manufacturing facilities. Good C&I prospecting area. NOAC switched from Energy Harbor to Dynegy June 2025. Dynegy contract (8.63¢→9.75¢) ended May 2026. New NOAC contract terms being finalized.

name: Lucas County Unincorporated
takeaway: Lucas County unincorporated areas are nominally in the NOAC coalition but rural corners may not be enrolled. Verify address before assuming NOAC coverage applies.
hook: If your accounts are in unincorporated Lucas County, NOAC might apply — but let's verify the service address first to be sure.
notes: NOAC includes Lucas County unincorporated as a member, but some rural and fringe addresses outside township enrollment may fall outside aggregation. Toledo Edison serves the area. Note: Bowling Green (Wood County) is a municipal utility — not part of NOAC and not eligible for competitive electric supply. NOAC switched from Energy Harbor to Dynegy June 2025. Dynegy contract (8.63¢→9.75¢) ended May 2026. New NOAC contract terms being finalized.
